blogs.title: Mining Gold from the Web: How DeepSeekMath Built a Massive Math Corpus
blogs.description: Ever wonder how AI models learn complex math? This post explores the innovative 'data mining' pipeline used to create the DeepSeekMath Corpus. We'll break down how researchers used an iterative process—combining fastText classifiers and human annotations—to sift through 120 billion tokens of web data to find the perfect training material, and why web data actually outperformed academic papers.

blogs.title: Why Code is the Secret Ingredient to AI Math Reasoning
blogs.description: Does learning to program make you a better mathematician? In the world of LLMs, the answer is a resounding yes. This blog post explores the fascinating finding that starting with a code-trained model (DeepSeek-Coder) provided the perfect foundation for mastering math, proving that the logic of programming is deeply intertwined with the logic of mathematics.

blogs.title: Doing More with Less: How GRPO is Revolutionizing AI Training
blogs.description: Training massive models usually requires an astronomical amount of memory. This post introduces Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a clever new reinforcement learning algorithm that achieves GPT-4 level performance by removing the 'critic' model used in standard PPO. We'll explain how this 'group-based' approach makes training smarter, faster, and much more efficient.

blogs.title: The Unified Theory of AI Learning: Understanding SFT, DPO, and GRPO
blogs.description: The world of AI training is full of confusing acronyms like SFT, DPO, and PPO. This blog post simplifies the complexity by presenting the researchers' 'Unified Paradigm.' We'll explain how all these methods are actually different variations of the same core concept—Data, Rewards, and Algorithms—and what that means for the future of building smarter AI.

blogs.title: Does RL Actually Make AI Smarter? Decoding the 'Robustness' Factor
blogs.description: When we use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to improve math scores, are we actually making the model more 'intelligent' or just better at picking the right answer? This post dives into the researchers' findings on 'Maj@K' vs 'Pass@K' scores to explain how RL helps models become more robust and reliable in their reasoning.
